source.title: Enhancing SignSGD: Small-Batch Convergence Analysis and a Hybrid Switching Strategy

record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out accuracy for Adam and SGD on CIFAR-100, using a different optimizer setup from the cited adaptive-optimizer comparisons.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR-100 Adam and well-tuned SGD results bear on V4. Dithering and hybrid-switch results are the paper’s new methods; they are not separate rows for V4. Convergence analysis and cited prior results are not empirical results on the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adam and SGD held-out accuracy on ResNet-18/CIFAR-100, bearing on V4 through its own results. The tuning budget is unspecified, so it does not establish the limited-tuning condition.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors also conclude that calibrated switching beats both pure SGD and SignSGD-M on CIFAR-10, while mitigating SignSGD-M stagnation on CIFAR-100 without matching SGD. They present small-batch convergence theory and pre-sign dithering as additional contributions; all experiments use a single worker.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies SignSGD improvements and includes an Adam versus well-tuned SGD comparison; it does not reproduce the cited adaptive-optimizer studies’ broader benchmark comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset: the paper reports optimizer comparisons on CIFAR-100 and CIFAR-10, but Adam’s table entry is only reported for CIFAR-100.

fits_no_version.finding: Switching from SignSGD-M to SGD reaches 92.18% on CIFAR-10 versus SGD's 91.38%, but reaches approximately 72% on CIFAR-100 versus SGD's 77%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Projection-calibrated switching from sign-based updates to SGD can improve held-out accuracy, with benefits depending on the dataset; this does not test switching from Adam to SGD.

record.problems: The optimizer comparison relevant to V4 is limited to a single CIFAR-100 setting; Adam’s tuning procedure is not stated, and uncertainty estimates are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results left out. Other Table I results concern SignSGD variants and a hybrid method rather than the adaptive-optimizer comparison named in V4.

A documented limited-tuning budget; broader-tuning comparisons; training-performance comparisons; other adaptive optimizers and language benchmarks; decoupled weight decay; switching specifically from Adam to SGD.

record.verdict_notes: Unspecified tuning and absent uncertainty estimates constrain interpretation but do not constitute results limiting V4. Figure 1 reports a shared learning-rate schedule; Table I distinguishes separately tuned schedules for the dithering and hybrid experiments. SignSGD comparisons and small-batch stationarity theory do not independently test V4 or V5.
